original_question: Consider the degenerate complex Monge-Ampere flow (omega_t + dd^c phi_t)^n = exp(dot(phi_t) + F(t, x, phi)) mu(t, x) on [0, T] x X, where omega_t is a continuous family of semi-positive big (1,1)-forms bounded below by a fixed semi-positive big form, F is continuous and nondecreasing in the last variable, and mu is a bounded continuous volume form. If u is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution and v is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity supersolution with u <= v on the parabolic boundary {0} x X, determine whether u <= v holds on all of [0, T] x X.
target_in_paper: Question 45 (Eyssidieux-Guedj-Zeriahi) in Section 6.4.3, Viscosity comparison principles, which asks whether the general comparison principle holds for viscosity subsolutions and supersolutions of the degenerate complex Monge–Ampère flow on a compact Kähler space. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact flow under discussion, the continuity and monotonicity assumptions on F, the bounded continuous volume form μ, the lower bound on the family ω_t by a fixed semi-positive big form, the bounded upper/lower semicontinuous viscosity subsolution/supersolution framework, the boundary condition u≤v on the initial parabolic boundary, and the desired global conclusion u≤v everywhere. These are the core ingredients of Question 45. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient space should be specified as a compact Kähler space X, not an arbitrary unspecified X. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The paper fixes T∈]0,+∞] and denotes the flow domain by X_T=[0,T[×X; restoring this makes the question paper-faithful and stand-alone. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The setup explicitly states that ω=ω(t,x) is a continuous family of semi-positive and big (1,1)-forms on X, uniformly bounded below by a fixed semi-positive and big (1,1)-form θ. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The paper writes F as F(t,z,r), continuous on [0,T[×X×R and nondecreasing in r; the full domain of definition should be stated. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
The nonnegativity μ(t,z)≥0 should be made explicit, even though it is implicit in the phrase volume form. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
The paper identifies the relevant parabolic boundary here with the initial slice {0}×X. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
The paper poses this as an open comparison-principle question, not as an already-settled theorem. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a compact Kähler space, let T∈(0,+∞], and set X_T=[0,T)×X. Consider the degenerate complex Monge–Ampère flow (ω_t+dd^cφ_t)^n=exp(∂_tφ(t,x)+F(t,x,φ(t,x)))μ(t,x) on X_T, where ω_t=ω(t,·) is a continuous family of semi-positive and big (1,1)-forms on X satisfying ω_t≥θ for some fixed semi-positive and big (1,1)-form θ, F:[0,T)×X×R→R is continuous and nondecreasing in its last variable, μ(t,x)≥0 is a bounded continuous volume form, and φ_t:=φ(t,·). Does the following comparison principle hold: if u is a bounded upper semicontinuous viscosity subsolution and v is a bounded lower semicontinuous viscosity supersolution of this flow on X_T, with u≤v on the parabolic boundary {0}×X, must one have u≤v on all of X_T? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the paper’s exact open problem in the viscosity section. The introduction says the last section collects open questions arising in the viscosity approach to degenerate elliptic and parabolic Monge–Ampère equations, and Section 6.4.3 then introduces precisely this family of flows and states Question 45 in essentially the same terms as your draft. The main adjustments needed are to restore the exact ambient setting (compact Kähler space), the paper’s time-cylinder notation X_T=[0,T)×X with T∈(0,+∞], the explicit nonnegativity of μ, and the fact that this is posed as an open question whose general case remained open in the paper, though special cases and the pseudoconvex-domain case were already known. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
